hints: Start with the easiest match. Helicase unwinds the parental double helix, so ask yourself which function phrase describes making the two strands free to be copied.
Now match the other easy one. DNA polymerase synthesises a strand of DNA, so remember it can only add new DNA nucleotides to the 3' end of a growing chain.
walkthrough:
**Link each role to its purpose**

Think about what each action achieves. Unwinding separates the helix, breaking and rejoining relieves strain, stabilising stops rejoining, and synthesising builds a new strand.

**Match helicase and DNA polymerase first**

Helicase unwinds the parental DNA double helix, so its function is that it makes strands available as templates. DNA polymerase synthesises a strand of DNA, so its function is that it adds DNA nucleotides to the 3' end of a growing polynucleotide strand.

**Match the last two proteins**

Topoisomerase breaks and rejoins the DNA strands, so its function is that it enables tension caused by unwinding to be released. Single-strand binding protein binds to separated strands to stabilise them, so its function is that it prevents original strands reforming complementary base pairs. Only row D has all four correct.

options.A: All four are mixed up. Helicase does not build the new strand, and DNA polymerase does not just make templates available.
options.B: DNA polymerase is correct here, but helicase is given the topoisomerase job and topoisomerase is given the binding protein job.
options.C: Helicase is given the topoisomerase job, and the other three proteins are also shifted into the wrong columns.
options.D: Perfect match. Helicase makes templates available, topoisomerase releases tension, binding protein prevents reforming base pairs, and polymerase adds nucleotides to the 3' end.
